Assessment.source_text: having listened to your story, I think you're probably suffering from what we call gastroenteritis

Assessment.content: Gastroenteritis typically lasts about three to five days and improves.
Assessment.source_text: normally lasts about three to five days, and gets better.

Plan_of_Care.content: Increase oral fluid intake to aid recovery.
Plan_of_Care.source_text: the things you can do to really help yourself get better soon, um are you can drink plenty of fluids. Really try and flush the toxins out of your body.

Plan_of_Care.content: Use oral rehydration solution (Dioralyte) to replace lost minerals and vitamins.
Plan_of_Care.source_text: Uh, you can get things from the pharmacy, which is called Dioralyte, which can help replenish any uh minerals and vitamins you may have lost. Uh, it's called Dioralyte. Um it's, it's a, it's a type of fluid replacement drink.

Plan_of_Care.content: Take paracetamol if feeling feverish or weak.
Plan_of_Care.source_text: Um, you can take some Paracetamol if you're feeling feverish and weak.

Plan_of_Care.content: Continue time off work for the next day or two until improvement.
Plan_of_Care.source_text: I would probably advise you to continue taking time off work for next day or two, until you get better.

Plan_of_Care.content: Do not return to work until diarrhea-free for 24 to 48 hours.
Plan_of_Care.source_text: normally you have to be diarrhea-free for about twenty four to forty eight hours, before you return back to work.

Follow_up_Information.content: If not improved by next week, return for review.
Follow_up_Information.source_text: And if you're still not better next week, I want you to come back and see me.
